extracted.intended_audience: researchers, institutional research administrators, and grants offices preparing or administering NSF proposals and awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, submitting, and administering proposals and awards for the U.S. National Science Foundation, including proposal contents, format, eligibility, merit review criteria, award types, and post-award requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criteria — Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: One of NSF's core merit review criteria listed under 'Merit Review Criteria' as 'Intellectual Merit'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators assess the potential of the proposed activity to advance knowledge and understanding within its own field or across different fields. (Referenced as a primary review criterion in Chapter III: NSF Proposal Processing and Review.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criteria — Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: One of NSF's core merit review criteria listed under 'Merit Review Criteria' as 'Broader Impacts'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators assess the potential of the proposed activity to benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes (e.g., broadening participation, education, public engagement). (Referenced as a primary review criterion in Chapter III: NSF Proposal Processing and Review.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF's overarching 'Merit Review Principles' that guide proposal evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles address how merit review is to be conducted (e.g., fairness, balance, transparency, reliance on researchers and experts). See Chapter III for full principles and related implementation guidance used by program officers and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Format Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Conformance requirements for proposal preparation including 'Format of the Proposal', 'Proposal Pagination Instructions', and 'Proposal Font, Spacing and Margin Requirements'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must follow NSF-specified formatting (fonts, spacing, margins, pagination) and other layout rules. Nonconforming proposals risk return without review or sanction. See Part I, Chapter II for exact formatting specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Proposal Content and Sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory sections of a proposal: Cover Sheet, Project Summary, Table of Contents, Project Description (including Results from Prior NSF Support), References Cited, Biographical Sketch(es), Budget and Budget Justification, Current and Pending Support, Facilities/Equipment/Other Resources, Special Information and Supplementary Documentation, Appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each section has content expectations and possible page limits; failure to include required sections or required content (e.g., Results from Prior NSF Support where applicable) can affect review and eligibility. See Part I: Sections of the Proposal for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description — Page Limitations and URLs
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Description content and its page limitations, including rules on inclusion of URLs within the Project Description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Description must stay within specified page limits and adhere to rules about external URLs (URLs may not be used to circumvent page limits or provide critical content). See Chapter II for exact page limits and URL policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Required elements of Biographical Sketch(es), including (a) Professional Preparation, (b) Appointments, (c) Products, and (d) Synergistic Activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biographical sketches must include specified sections and information structured per PAPPG rules; this standardization supports reviewer evaluation of investigator qualifications and relevant outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget components and related policies: Salaries and Wages (including Senior Personnel and Administrative/Clerical policies), Fringe Benefits, Equipment, Travel (domestic and foreign), Participant Support, Materials and Supplies, Publication/Dissemination, Consultant/Professional Service Costs, Computer Services, Subawards, Other Direct Costs, Indirect (F&A) Costs, Amount of This Request, Cost Sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgets must follow NSF rules for allowability, allocation, and documentation. Specific policies (e.g., administrative/clerical salaries policy, prior approvals, pre-award costs) govern whether costs are allowable and how they are presented. See Part I: Budget and Budget Justification and Part II: Allowability of Costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards governing which project costs are allowable, unallowable, or require prior written approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment of entertainment, meals, alcoholic beverages; pre-award and post-end costs; maximum obligations; and procedures for prior approvals. Conflicts with other guidelines and special considerations are covered in Part II, Chapter X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May Submit Proposals / Eligibility of Proposers
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of entities eligible to submit proposals: Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs), non-profit non-academic organizations, for-profit organizations, state and local governments, unaffiliated individuals, foreign organizations, other federal agencies; with special instructions for international branch campuses of U.S. IHEs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility rules define allowable proposers and any special submission instructions. Some program solicitations may modify eligibility requirements. See Chapter I.F for categories of proposers.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Submit Proposals — Deadlines and Exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission timing rules: Target Dates, Deadline Dates, Submission Windows, and Special Exceptions to NSF’s Deadline Date Policy (e.g., natural disasters, closure of NSF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must be submitted by program-specific dates unless an approved exception applies. Program solicitations and divisional websites list deadlines and target dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Submit Proposals — Electronic and Administrative Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submission requirements and administrative identifiers: electronic requirements, submission instructions, DUNS (DUNS Numbers)/SAM registration, NSF ID, and interaction with Grants.gov where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers must register and maintain organizational identifiers (e.g., DUNS/SAM) and follow the specified electronic submission system (FastLane, Research.gov, or Grants.gov) technical and administrative instructions to ensure receipt and processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Submissions and Proposal Pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission types: Letters of Intent, Preliminary Proposals, Invite/Not Invite, Encourage/Discourage, Full Proposals, and program-specific variations (e.g., RAPID, EAGER, RAISE, GOALI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different submission types have different requirements, review processes, and expectations. Program solicitations may require or permit particular submission types; follow solicitation-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Processing and Review Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF proposal receipt, processing, reviewer selection, merit review, provision of review information to PIs, and potential release of grantee proposal information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes how proposals are assigned, reviewed by external reviewers and program officers, how review summaries are delivered to PIs, and NSF’s policies on release of proposal information under applicable regulations and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results from Prior NSF Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to include 'Results from Prior NSF Support' where applicable in the Project Description or other designated sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For investigators with relevant prior NSF support, proposers must provide prior award information and results to allow reviewers to assess productivity and stewardship of prior funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborators & Other Affiliations Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure requirements for collaborators and other affiliations for proposal personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate disclosure supports reviewer selection and conflict-of-interest determinations. Specific formats and instructions are in Part I.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Suggested Reviewers / Reviewers Not to Include
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional/required lists where proposers may suggest reviewers or identify reviewers the proposer prefers not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists are used by program officers in selecting reviewers but are not binding; conflicts of interest and balance considerations still govern selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary or Privileged Information Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for marking or handling proprietary/privileged information included in proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers must follow PAPPG procedures for identifying proprietary information; improper markings or overuse may affect review or disclosure under FOIA and public reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and Types of Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of award instruments and types: Grant Agreement, Standard Grant, Continuing Grant, Cost Reimbursement Award, Fixed Amount Award, Cooperative Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each award type has different legal and administrative implications (e.g., level of NSF involvement, accountability basis—costs vs. performance). Choice of instrument affects proposal/award terms and post-award management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperative Agreement — Substantial Involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and examples for when an award is a cooperative agreement rather than a grant, emphasizing 'substantial involvement' by NSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial involvement may include prior agency approval requirements, special reporting, frequency/type of project plans, deliverables, and other monitoring actions. Examples include management of research centers, large facilities, major instrumentation development, and activities requiring NSF coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Fundable Research / Research Not Normally Supported
rubrics_metrics.description: Areas NSF does not normally support: technical assistance, pilot plant efforts, research requiring security classification, development of products for commercial marketing, market research for a particular project/invention, research with disease-related goals (etiology, diagnosis, treatment), animal models for disease or drug testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist where work advances core engineering or computer science knowledge (e.g., bioengineering/information technology applying engineering or CS principles to problems in biology/medicine) or for assistive technologies for persons with disabilities. Proposers should consult program offices for potential exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee Responsibilities and NSF Monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation of responsibilities: grantees are wholly responsible for conducting project activities and preparing results for publication; NSF monitors progress and compliance and provides peer review summaries to PIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF does not assume responsibility for findings or their interpretation. Post-award monitoring, reporting, and compliance duties are detailed in Part II and relevant award terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Requirements and Closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical and administrative reporting requirements: Annual Project Reports, Final Project Report, Project Outcomes Report for the General Public, compliance with technical reporting requirements, and grant closeout procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely and complete submission of required reports is required for compliance and continued funding; details and formats are provided in Part II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee Standards: Conflict of Interest and Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing grantee standards including conflict of interest policies and expectations for Responsible Conduct of Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must have appropriate policies and training in place; NSF responsibilities and institutional responsibilities are outlined in Part II. Noncompliance can affect award actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Proposal Types and Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Program-specific proposal categories and targeted mechanisms: RAPID, EAGER, RAISE, GOALI, Ideas Lab, Facilitation Awards for Scientists and Engineers with Disabilities (FASED), Conference Proposal, Equipment Proposal, Travel Proposal, Center Proposal, Research Infrastructure Proposal, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each special type has unique preparation and review requirements; proposers must follow the specific chapter or solicitation instructions for those mechanisms (e.g., FASED instructions in Chapter II.D.4).
